abstract: Histone post-translational modifications and gene expression jointly shape cellular identity and activity. However, systematically assessing their heterogeneity and functional interdependence requires high-quality multimodal single-cell readouts, whose generation still faces significant technological challenges. Here, we developed TrES-seq (transcriptional and epigenetic state sequencing), a method that integrates scRNA-seq with species-specific nanobody Tn5 fusion proteins to jointly profile RNA and two histone modifications in the same cells and across multiple samples. In human tonsils, single-cell H3K27ac, H3K27me3, H3K9me3, and RNA data in >25,000 cells revealed a one-to-many relationship where heterogeneous transcriptional states shared similar epigenetic profiles. For example, naive and memory B cells were transcriptionally different but epigenetically indistinguishable, while the epigenetic status of enhancers but not promoters separated germinal center from naive and memory B cells. Moreover, naturally occurring and treatment-induced cell state transitions revealed broad transcriptional changes occurring among genes that already exhibited and retained an epigenetically active state. Overall, TrES-seq provides a robust and cost-effective platform to determine how epigenetic states influence transcriptional heterogeneity, shaping cell phenotypes and function in different physiological and pathological contexts.
